title: U.S. House · Alabama's 5th Congressional District
area: North Alabama, including Huntsville, Madison, Decatur, and the Tennessee Valley.

context.text: Incumbent Dale Strong (R) advanced without a primary after his Republican primary was canceled. Andrew Sneed defeated Candice Duvieilh 78.4% to 21.6% in the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary runoff, after the two advanced from a three-way May 19 primary. Cook Political Report rated the district R+15 for 2026.

candidates.name: Dale Strong
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after the primary was canceled.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 5th Congressional District (since 2023)

summary.text: Dale Strong is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Alabama's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A lifelong first responder in Monrovia, he served 26 years in Madison County government, first as a county commissioner and then as the commission's first Republican chairman. In the 119th Congress he serves on the Appropriations Committee, where he is Vice Chair of the Commerce, Justice, Science Subcommittee, and chairs a Homeland Security subcommittee.

background.text: Born in Monrovia, Alabama, and graduated from Sparkman High School (1988, per Wikipedia). He is the son of a founding member of the Monrovia Fire-Rescue Department.
Earned a B.S. in business administration from Athens State University, and an EMT license from the University of Alabama in Huntsville, according to Wikipedia.

According to his official biography, he has spent his adult life as a first responder: a junior volunteer firefighter and 911 dispatcher who has 35 years of service as an EMT and 41 years as a volunteer firefighter. Wikipedia adds earlier jobs in public relations at First Alabama Bank and as a sales representative for Solvay.

First elected to the Madison County Commission in 1996, according to Wikipedia, as the youngest elected Republican official in Alabama at the time; his official biography says he served in local government for 26 years.
Elected chairman of the Madison County Commission in 2012, the first Republican to hold the post; he served until resigning on January 2, 2023.

Won the 2022 Republican primary for the open seat of Rep. Mo Brooks, defeating Casey Wardynski in a June 21 runoff with about 63%, then won the general election with about 67% against Democrat Kathy Warner-Stanton, according to Wikipedia.

Sworn in January 2023. Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, with subcommittee roles as Vice Chair of Commerce, Justice, Science, plus Transportation, Housing and Urban Development and Legislative Branch, and chairs the Homeland Security Emergency Management and Technology Subcommittee.
According to his official biography, he is married to Laura Toney Strong and they have two children, Whitney and Harrison.

priorities.text: Describes himself as a "Trump Conservative" who says taking Republican control of Congress is central to his campaign.
Says cutting wasteful federal spending and reducing the national debt should be a top priority, pointing to his record balancing the Madison County budget as commission chairman.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a pro-life Christian who will "stand up for the unborn."
Says he is a lifetime NRA member who will fight for Second Amendment rights.
Says "raising taxes is not an option" and that cutting wasteful federal spending must be a top priority.
positions.quote: Raising taxes is not an option.

positions.summary: Says he will always support law enforcement and, as Madison County Commission chairman, raised starting pay for sheriff's deputies.
Campaign website calls for stronger border security and criticizes Congress for what he describes as inadequate enforcement.

record.text: Chairs the House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Emergency Management and Technology and serves as Vice Chair of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Served as Vice Chairman of the Homeland Security Subcommittee on Emergency Preparedness, Response and Recovery, and on the House Committee on Armed Services and Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

candidates.name: Andrew Sneed
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary runoff, 78.4% to 21.6%, over Candice Duvieilh.

summary.text: Andrew Sneed is a Huntsville small-business owner and the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 5th Congressional District. A Huntsville native and Boston University graduate, he worked in New York restaurants before returning to Alabama and training as a plumber; he founded a mechanical-contracting company in 2019. He has not previously held office and says he is running on affordability, health care, and government-accountability reforms.

background.text: According to his campaign website, born and raised in Huntsville, the son of a local attorney and a school teacher/administrator; grew up on the family farm outside town and in Blossomwood.
Graduated from Lee High School in 1998 and earned a BFA from Boston University in 2003.

Spent seven years in New York City after college, working in the restaurant business, before returning to Alabama in 2010. Ballotpedia lists past work as an actor, stuntman, bartender, farmer, and restaurant manager, among others.
At age 32, started over as a $10-an-hour plumber's helper and worked up over about seven years to master plumber and gas fitter, per his campaign website.
Founded his company, Whole Home Solutions, in 2019; his campaign website says it has six work trucks and seven employees (his Ballotpedia survey says a team of eight).

Entered the 2026 Democratic primary for the 5th District; no candidate won a majority on May 19, and he advanced to a June 16 runoff against Candice Dollar Duvieilh, in which the Alabama Democratic Conference endorsed him.

According to his campaign website, he is married and the father of three daughters. He has described a 'Balance / Accountability' pledge that includes term limits and prohibiting stock trading in Congress.

priorities.text: Affordability, healthcare, job stability, and public education, including repealing tariffs and reforming the tax code so that wealthy earners "pay their fair share."
Restoring Affordable Care Act subsidies, comprehensive insurance reform, and revitalizing rural healthcare.

Government-accountability reforms, including a personal "Balance/Accountability" pledge covering congressional term limits, repealing Citizens United, banning stock trading by members of Congress, and an enforceable Supreme Court ethics code.

positions.summary: Says he is committed to restoring ACA subsidies, comprehensive insurance reform, and revitalizing rural healthcare.
Says changing the tax code to ensure the wealthy pay their fair share is part of his platform.
Lists "repealing harmful tariffs" among his proposed solutions to affordability issues.
